_what: RANK'S ERROR BAR — the same bytes through five independent blind seats.
RULED (Rafe, 2026-09-08): 'Measure the comparator's noise floor: same bytes through five
seats, record the flip rate, publish it as rank's error bar.' LAW: a gate's binding term
must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample (bible §13.13).
THIS IS THE NUMBER THAT BELONGS BESIDE THE THRESHOLD wherever the threshold is quoted. A
bar without it is a bar nobody can size.
ruling: PASS-INSTALL rests on a single rank sample and flipped on identical bytes — impeachment upheld. ... Measure the comparator's noise floor: same bytes through five seats, record the flip rate, publish it as rank's error bar. — Rafe, 2026-09-08
reading: TWO OF FIVE SEATS DISAGREE WITH THE MAJORITY — a 40% flip rate on unchanged bytes.
The build placed 1st three times and 3rd twice in a four-frame deck, with the seeded
reference taking the other position each time. This is the comparator PASS-INSTALL binds
on, and it is why the ruling put a three-seat majority in front of it.
⚠ AND THE SECOND COLUMN MATTERS MORE FOR THIS BUILD. Three of five seats FLAGGED the
build. 'No unrouted flags from any' is not a majority test, so on this evidence the
A+B+C build does not clear the vote on flags even when it clears it on rank.
⚠ CORRELATED PLANTS. The axis-matched morgue set for combined/tonal has exactly one
member, so all five seats drew the same plant. Every seat caught it, but those catches
⚠ THE PLANT OUTRANKED THE BUILD in at least one seat's deck. Recorded, never scored (§4):
it is a statement about the build, not about the judge.

_what: THE PANEL OF THREE IS ITSELF NOISY — measured 2026-09-08 on a second frozen frame.
The three-seat panel was the remedy for a single seat's flip rate. It has now been run
TWICE ON IDENTICAL BYTES and returned opposite answers on the term that gates the
install:
r002-polish-198-halo   NOT BELOW the reference in 3 of 3 seats   -> install bar met
r003-polish-198-halo   NOT BELOW the reference in 1 of 3 seats   -> no majority
Same picture, byte-identical: the round's own progress line reads 'picture moved mean
0.000 / worst 0 luminance levels'. Six independent seats in total on this frame.
⚠ THE BAR IS NOT RE-TUNED HERE. LOOP-PROCESS §8: a bar found wanting mid-run is held
frozen, cleared honestly and impeached in the same report, never adjusted once the
answer is visible. r003 is the round that describes this tree, r003 says no majority,
and nothing installed. Choosing r002 because it agrees with me is the exact move the
rule exists to forbid, and a third panel run after seeing r003 would be the same move
wearing a better name.
WHAT THE NUMBER ACTUALLY SAYS. Seat-level, this build is not below its reference in
4 of 6 seats — p = 0.667. A majority of three drawn from that lands not-below with
probability p^3 + 3p^2(1-p) = 0.296 + 0.444 = 0.741, so ABOUT ONE PANEL IN FOUR will
report 'no majority' on a build that is genuinely 2-of-3 at seat level. The panel
narrowed the error bar; it did not remove it, and it cannot: it is three samples of a
statistic whose per-sample flip rate is 40%.
This is recorded as evidence for whoever rules on the bar next, not as an argument for
a particular ruling. Options a ruling might weigh, none of them taken here: more seats
(the error falls as 1/sqrt(n) and five was already ruled once); a rank margin rather
than a strict majority; or accepting that a polish increment this small is simply below
the comparator's resolution, which would make 'not worse' unmeasurable and would move
the install decision to the item's own measured exit alone.
